note: Adapted from the species-level description in Roonwal & Chhotani 1989, Fauna of India: Isoptera; the original is in English. Only the soldier is described, and figure caption 308 also refers to the soldier. OCR problems: the sentence break at lines 24—25 ('more slender, / incurved distal part') runs across a page, and the sense has been joined as in the original; the original contains OCR corruptions such as 'IS-segmented', read here from context as '15-segmented'.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head subrectangular, massive and thick, strongly hypognathous; compound eyes and ocelli absent; antennae 14—15-segmented; pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe far longer than the posterior lobe, the anterior margin convex, without a median notch; tarsus 3-segmented, tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Both the alate and the worker are recorded as unknown in the original.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head and body brown, with a reddish or smoky tinge; the apex of the abdomen pale yellow, a white longitudinal stripe extending from the pronotum to the 9th abdominal tergite. Head densely covered with short hairs and with a few long bristles; postclypeus with the same pilosity as the head; labrum with a few slightly longer hairs. Head subrectangular (head length (length to base of mandibles) 2.72—2.91 mm, maximum head width 2.66—2.93 mm), large and thick, strongly hypognathous, the sides slightly convex; posterior margin slightly concave; Y-shaped suture faint. Compound eyes and ocelli absent. Antennae 14—15-segmented (when 15-segmented, segment 2 twice as long as segment 3). Clypeus and frons distinctly separated. Labrum small, ligulate, slightly longer than wide. Mandibles stout, shorter than the head (length 1.51—1.68 mm), with a few fine hairs at the base; with a broad basal plate and a narrower incurved distal part, and a large tooth on the inner margin between the two halves. Postmentum short (length 1.12—1.27 mm), clavate, inflated at the apical third. Pronotum hairy, much smaller than the head (length 0.69—0.77, width 1.06—1.18 mm), strongly saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe far longer than the posterior lobe; anterior margin convex, without a median notch; posterior margin slightly concave. Tarsus 3-segmented; tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The original records both the alate (Imago) and the worker (Worker) as unknown; type locality Adampur, Bangladesh.
